edges.description: Hair-cell functional impairment precedes degeneration in the mouse. This is informative for the progressive subset of human disease but does not reproduce every congenital or stable clinical presentation.
edges.limitations: A mouse point allele standing in for a range of human variants. The correspondence of a particular human genotype's severity to the samba phenotype has not been established, and the human onset range is wide.

edges.description: Direct measurements show near-normal first-week inner-hair-cell mechanotransduction currents followed by severe impairment at P11. Gross bundle organization and tip links are preserved at these ages, despite modest shortening of lower stereociliary rows.
edges.limitations: Mouse timing and allele effects cannot be assumed for all human variants. Residual hearing in T1308X animals may reflect alternative splicing; nearby genetic modifiers were not excluded. Maintained Harmonin and LHFPL5 do not establish that all channel components remain normally localized.
edges.source: Loxhd1 PLAT10 samba and T1308X mouse comparison

edges.description: Large-scale deletion establishes that LOXHD1 maintains TMC1 at the lower tip-link insertion. Remaining TMC1 redistributes along stereociliary shafts, while TMC2 localization is preserved. Inner-hair-cell currents are already reduced at P7 and become more severely impaired at P11.
edges.limitations: This engineered large deletion does not represent the full spectrum of human alleles. Some residual currents remain; mild heterozygote mouse threshold changes do not establish dominant human DFNB77.

edges.description: Direct inner-hair-cell recordings measure reduced currents at P7 and P11 after complete deletion.
edges.limitations: Developmental mouse timing and a complete deletion cannot predict the course of every human allele.

edges.description: A naturally occurring recessive missense variant segregated with congenital or early-onset bilateral deafness in Rottweilers. Four affected littermates lacked auditory brainstem responses when tested.
edges.limitations: Variant segregation and hearing tests support a large-animal model, but this study did not measure mechanotransduction or hair-cell histology in the genotyped dogs. Histological degeneration described in earlier ungenotyped Rottweilers cannot be attributed definitively to this allele. Progression from partial loss to deafness was inferred from owner reports and remains unconfirmed.

nodes.description: Two sisters had an auditory neuropathy spectrum presentation, with abnormal or absent synchronized brainstem responses despite detectable cochlear microphonics and limited early otoacoustic emissions. Their cousin had residual brainstem waveforms with progressive hearing loss. These electrophysiological findings are consistent with a presynaptic hair-cell disorder but do not establish the site of every lesion or a population frequency.

nodes.description: Cochlear implantation can provide useful auditory and language outcomes in selected individuals with severe-to-profound LOXHD1-associated hearing loss. Benefit is reported in an Ashkenazi Jewish series, four assessed Japanese recipients, and two sisters with an auditory-neuropathy presentation. These small observational reports do not establish a universal response rate or a genotype-specific optimal implantation age.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic LOXHD1 variants impair a stereociliary protein containing up to fifteen PLAT repeats. The molecular consequence is allele dependent: missense variants need not remove the protein, and nonsense-associated alternative splicing can preserve part of its coding sequence in a mouse model. Epitope-tagged mouse LOXHD1 is enriched at the tips of the shorter, transducing stereocilia. Earlier staining along the stereociliary membrane used an antibody whose specificity could not be confirmed with a complete null control.

nodes.description: Mechanically evoked receptor currents decline in LOXHD1-mutant cochlear hair cells before gross bundle disruption. PLAT10 missense and targeted truncating mouse alleles retain near-control currents at P7 but show severe reduction at P11, with unchanged measured residual-current kinetics at P9. A complete Loxhd1 deletion already reduces currents at P7 and leaves small residual currents at P11. Tip links and selected tip-link proteins can remain present despite TMC1 mislocalization; their presence does not demonstrate an intact channel complex. Human onset and progression cannot be inferred directly from these postnatal mouse time points.

nodes.description: Remaining TMC1 molecules progressively redistribute away from the lower tip-link insertion along stereociliary shafts. This spatial separation limits transmission of sound-induced forces to the channels. LOXHD1 co-immunoprecipitates with TMC1, CIB2, LHFPL5 and PCDH15-CD2 in heterologous cells, but not with TMC2 or TMIE in the tested assays. These associations and mouse localization support a stabilizing connection; they do not establish the exact direct-binding topology or show that every human variant disrupts the same interaction.
